description: PostgreSQL health metric catalog. Derived from dbi services scoring framework v0.30+. Metric semantics validated against PostgreSQL 14 → 18 (PG 14 default checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9 is the floor; per-metric min_pg_version gates feature-specific metrics).
release_notes:
v1.14.0 (2026-10-08): Absolute target. From package 1.17.0 an uncollected check counts 0 points, so the checks the collector omits because they do not apply now say so: SEC-2.3 ssl_cert_days_remaining applies only with SSL on (like SEC-2.2); CAP-1.3 tablespace_headroom (no non-default tablespace), PER-2.16 query_store_mode, PER-2.17 wait_sampling_mode, PER-2.18 intelligent_tuning (extension not loaded), CAP-2.9 pgbouncer_min_pool_size and CAP-2.10 pgbouncer_ignore_startup_params (left at their default) and PER-4.4 synchronous_standby_names (empty is correct for asynchronous-only replication; a declared synchronous standby without names is caught by PG-CR-HA-1) apply only when their value is present. Until the collector tells "does not apply" from "could not collect", a collection failure on these reads as not applicable. v1.13.0 (2026-09-28): One ruler, a target per estate. Every check counts for every estate; a declared target never switches a check off. The new optional_when field names the declared targets under which a check is not required: it then still earns or loses its own points, but leaves the target score and never triggers a criticality gate. Not required: BAK-1.1 archive_mode, the checks that judge archiving once it is on (BAK-1.2 archive_command, BAK-1.3 archive_failures, BAK-1.7 archive_timeout), BAK-1.5 summarize_wal and CHK-BAK-2 backup_tool_detection at a 24-hour RPO; BAK-3.1 external_backup_tool and BAK-3.2 pitr_enabled at a 24-hour RPO with an 8- or 24-hour RTO; BAK-3.3 backup_encryption and SEC-2.4 encryption_at_rest at a baseline posture; SEC-3.4 pgaudit_installed at a baseline or hardened posture (previously not judged at all outside a regulated posture); BAK-4.5 streaming_status and BAK-4.7 ha_standby_count with ha_topology=none; PER-4.4 synchronous_standby_names with none or async_standby; BAK-4.9 restore_time_estimate_minutes with a declared standby or cluster (previously not judged at all outside ha_topology=none). Undeclared estates are required to meet every check, so pgaudit and the restore estimate now count on them. The dump schedule no longer decides anything. BAK-1.3 archive_failures applies only with archiving on. PG-CR-HA-2 fires only on a collected streaming_status. SSL stays a floor on every environment: the four SSL checks carry the new floor flag, which the validators protect from optional_when. Remediations of BAK-4.9 and thirteen rules (BAK-CR-1, BAK-CR-1B, the recovery point, recovery time, security posture and HA topology rules) put fixing the practice first and name correcting an overclaimed declaration second, with its consequence; PG-CR-SECPOST-1 says SSL is required at every posture. "yes" is no longer an accepted rpo_target or rto_target value (it bypassed every coherence rule). The six declarations carry the new declared_target flag, echoed by the engine in context.declarations.
v1.12.0 (2026-09-03): PostgreSQL Technology Leader review (2026-09-03). Database size (CAP-1.1) becomes a capture metric feeding target coherence instead of a size ceiling; new BAK-4.8 restore_throughput_mb_s (attested) and BAK-4.9 restore_time_estimate_minutes (engine-derived, scored against the declared RTO rung, only without an HA topology); new rules PG-CR-RTO-3 and PG-CR-RTO-4 invalidate an RTO that a restore cannot meet on a standalone instance. SEC-3.4 pgaudit applies only under a declared regulated posture. Size-weighted bloat (CAP-3.2), temp files no longer blamed on work_mem alone (PER-2.9), provenance for the work_mem, effective_io_concurrency and autovacuum worker guidance. First technical_anchor and rationale fields. Adoption review (2026-09-23): maturity measurement-reviewed; BAK-2.2 ignores the declared RPO when archive_mode is on or always (new by_declaration.unless), falling back to its 24-hour base-backup freshness bound; new BAK-1.7 archive_timeout (advisory, applies with archiving on) must lie between 1 second and the declared RPO when no standby is streaming (streaming_status or ha_standby_count) and an RPO of 4 hours or less is declared, and new rule PG-CR-RPO-3 (warning, metric_zero on rpo_target) invalidates a 5- or 15-minute RPO that archive_timeout does not bound (2026-09-25); BAK-4.9 and PER-1.10 state what the restore estimate and the memory heuristic leave out. v1.8.0: R1 weight/placement/budget review. Budgets rebalanced net-zero per pillar: backup tools 4->3 / recovery 4->5; performance locks 4->3 / replication 4->5; future-proofing version 7->6 / config 3->5 / planning 6->5. PER-4.1 replication_lag_seconds important->critical with applies_when(streaming_status truthy OR ha_standby_count>=1) so standalone primaries are not gated for replication they never claimed. SEC-2.2 ssl_version gated on ssl_enabled (kills the vacuous TLS-floor pass on ssl=off instances); BAK-1.2 archive_command gated on archive_mode in [on,always]. BAK-5.2 offsite_backup advisory->important. First per-metric weight overrides (weight 0.5) on nine always-pass capture metrics: database_size, sync_standby, shared_buffers_bytes, intelligent_tuning, jit, work_mem_bytes, max_connections, synchronous_standby_names_count, synchronous_standby_names. HA-2.6 patroni_member_count moved capacity_connections->perf_replication. Rules: new PG-CR-RPO-2 (metric_zero + subcategory_cap 60 when an aggressive RPO has no WAL transport) and PG-CR-CONN-LOCK-1 (multi-deduction on connection saturation amplifying lock contention); BAK-CR-1/1B upgraded warning->critical with metric_zero(rpo_target). v1.7.0: full-audit content release (see catalog-review-postgresql-2026-06). Bug fixes: CAP-1.1 split into informational size (GB) + new CAP-1.7 disk_usage_pct (the old config scored GB against a percent threshold), CAP-1.2 growth-rate direction inverted (max->min days_to_full), PER-1.12 wal_buffers_ratio dropped (failed auto-tuned defaults above ~533MB shared_buffers; PER-1.11 floor raised to 8MB), CAP-3.7 gains an upper bound (1.5B). Thresholds: PER-2.11 [0,5000ms], CAP-1.5 4000, FUT-1.1 min 15. Dropped duplicates/low-signal: CHK-BAK-1, CAP-2.5, CAP-2.11, CHK-SEC-1, CHK-FUT-1; CHK-FUT-2 moved to capacity_maintenance as CAP-3.9. PER-4.1 critical->important pending engine applies_when. Refactors: identity repairs (BAK-5.2 offsite copy, CAP-4.3 scaling strategy, PER-2.4 manual review boolean, CAP-1.3/SEC-1.5 displays), PER-1.2 gains max 45%, PER-2.13 cpu_count-relative, PER-2.19 jit capture-only, PER-1.5/SEC-1.6 min_pg_version dropped, unit-field batch. Rules: BAK-CR-2 (-4 backup), BAK-CR-3 (-3 backup), SEC-CR-1 (-1 security_auth) now move scores; new BAK-CR-1B, PG-CR-HP-2, PG-CR-AV-1, PG-CR-POOL-1, PG-CR-CHK-1. 12 additions: disk_usage_pct, fsync, full_page_writes, idle_in_transaction_session_timeout, statement_timeout, temp_file_limit, track_counts, wal_compression, min_wal_size, autovacuum_max_workers, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit, logical_subscription_failures. v1.6.0: pgtune-style sizing + score-moving cross-metric relations. (a) 10 new sizing metrics — PER-1.8 huge_pages, PER-1.9 vm_nr_hugepages (manual input), PER-1.11 wal_buffers_bytes, PER-1.13 shared_buffers_bytes, PER-2.19 jit, PER-2.20 default_statistics_target (workload-profile-keyed), PER-2.21 work_mem_bytes, PER-2.22 max_connections (cap value), PER-4.2 synchronous_commit, PER-4.4 synchronous_standby_names. (b) 3 derived metrics computed by the engine: PER-1.10 memory_pressure_pct (shared_buffers + max_connections × work_mem / RAM), PER-1.12 wal_buffers_ratio, PER-4.3 synchronous_standby_names_count. (c) 5 new consistency rules now move the score — engine v1.6.0 implements applyAdjustments for subcategory_cap, subcategory_deduction, pillar_deduction: PG-CR-MEM-1, PG-CR-HP-1, PG-CR-SSD-1, PG-CR-OLAP-JIT-1 (demonstrates new workload_profile predicate operand), PG-CR-SYNC-1 (pillar_deduction, critical). v1.5.0 (PoC): seven hot metrics refactored to size-relative and workload-profile-keyed thresholds (PER-2.7, CAP-3.6, PER-2.9, PER-1.1, PER-1.4, PER-1.7, CAP-3.2). v1.4.0: introduces consistency_rules (findings-only in scoring-core v1.2). v1.1.0: subcategory point allocations within Capacity, Performance, and Future-Proofing pillars differ from the architecture specification (SCORING_SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md section 2.3); see docs/guides/metric-placement-review.md.
v1.9.0: Coherence expansion. Closed the RTO hole — PG-CR-RTO-1/2 link rto_target to recovery evidence (recovery_tested; PITR/streaming/backup-tool). New declared-target metrics: security_posture (SEC-4.7), growth_headroom_target (CAP-4.7), ha_topology (PER-4.6), each wired to coherence rules (SECPOST-1/2, CAP-1, HA-1/2). PG-CR-FUT-1 links upgrade_plan to versions_behind. 8 new rules (16->24), 3 new metrics (166->169). Declaration is never graded: every target enum is all-pass; penalties come only from coherence rules (metric_zero, +cap where the incoherence invalidates the subcategory).
v1.10.0: P0 production-relevance corrections. Thresholds: PER-1.2 shared_buffers band 20-45 -> 20-40 %RAM (docs cap useful range at 40), PER-3.2 deadlocks 0 -> 2 per 24h (occasional deadlocks are normal), FUT-1.1 min 15 -> 16 (convention: latest-minus-2, refreshed each catalog release; PG 18 latest, PG 13 EOL 2025-11), CAP-3.12 autovacuum cost limit 200 -> 1000 (200 = shipped default, SSD-era guidance 1000-4000), FUT-2.1 checkpoint_timeout 300 -> 900s and important -> advisory (300 = shipped default; 15-30 min guidance, read-mostly instances may deliberately stay low). Applicability gates: PER-2.10 effective_io_concurrency applies_when pg_version<=17 (PG 18 changed semantics/default to 16; AIO assessed by PER-1.6), CAP-2.3 idle_connections applies_when no connection_pooler declared (pooled idle is benign; unpooled idle = leaks). PER-2.14 max_parallel_workers_per_gather workload-profile-keyed (oltp min 0 = capture-only; disabling per-gather parallelism is legitimate OLTP tuning). New rule PG-CR-SECPOST-3: regulated posture + log_retention_days < 365 -> metric_zero(log_retention_days) (PCI DSS v4 wants 12 months; base threshold stays 90d for unregulated). Prose/metadata: PER-2.19 jit min_pg_version format fix 12 -> 120000 (never gated; server_version_num format), display 'JIT Compilation State' + PG19-aware remediation (PG 19 flips jit default to off; OLAP-JIT-1 remediation aligned), CHK-PER-2 weight 0.5 + large-table scoping caveat (collector verification handed to checker), SEC-1.1 Unix-socket exclusion note, FUT-2.2/CAP-3.11 reframed as floor checks, technology_version 17 -> 18. CIS references corrected to CIS PostgreSQL 16 Benchmark v1.0.0 numbering: SEC-1.1/1.2/1.3/1.6 -> 5.2, SEC-1.5 -> 5.3, SEC-2.1 -> 6.8, SEC-3.1 -> 3.1.20, SEC-3.2 -> 3.1.21, SEC-3.3 -> 3.1.25, SEC-4.1 -> 4.4, SEC-4.2 -> 4.2, SEC-4.3 -> 4.7; filled SEC-2.3 (6.8), SEC-3.4 (3.2), SEC-4.4 (4.5). Collector-side follow-ups: XID denominator, bloat estimation method, SSL socket exclusion, seq-scan large-table scoping, agent-absent not-assessed.
v1.10.1 (2026-07-21): Prose-only proofreading pass over display names, descriptions, remediations and consistency-rule texts for the TL review (typos, dangling clauses, tool-name casing, en-US spelling standardized). No threshold, weight, gate, or structural change. v1.11.0 (2026-07-22): Target-aware seeding + declaration hygiene (package 1.14.0). Seeded declaration-keyed thresholds (evaluation_config.by_declaration): BAK-2.2 last_backup_age_hours and PER-4.1 replication_lag_seconds derive their ceiling from the declared rpo_target (a declared 1-day RPO makes an 8-hour backup fine), and CAP-1.2 growth_rate derives its runway floor from growth_headroom_target; undeclared estates keep the 24h/60s/90-day absolutes, so nothing regresses without a declaration. FUT-3.1 upgrade_plan is now all-pass ('no'/'none' declared honestly scores full); the new PG-CR-FUT-2 rule deducts 1.5 from future_planning only when there is no plan AND the instance is more than two majors behind, the companion to PG-CR-FUT-1. No metric added or removed (169 metrics, 26 rules).

metrics.description: Whether WAL archiving (archive_mode) is on. Required for PITR; without it, only base backups exist.
metrics.remediation: Enable archive_mode in postgresql.conf: archive_mode = on

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'archive_mode'

metrics.rationale: Continuous WAL archiving is what makes a recovery point shorter than the backup interval possible. Not required when the declared RPO is 24 hours, which a daily backup meets: the check then leaves the target score but still counts, so archiving that is on earns its points and archiving that is off loses them. Undeclared estates are required to archive.

metrics.description: Whether a real archive_command is set. Empty or no-op commands disable archiving silently.
metrics.remediation: Configure archive_command to copy WAL files to backup storage

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'archive_command'

metrics.description: Count of WAL archiving failures in the last 24 hours. Repeated failures indicate destination or permission problems that block archiving.
metrics.remediation: Check archive_command permissions and destination storage availability

technical_anchor.query: SELECT failed_count, last_failed_time FROM pg_stat_archiver

metrics.description: WAL level adequacy. Archive/PITR needs at least 'replica'; logical replication needs 'logical'.
metrics.remediation: Set wal_level = replica (or logical) in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'wal_level'

metrics.description: Whether WAL summarization (summarize_wal) is on. Required for native incremental backups in PG 17+.
metrics.remediation: Enable summarize_wal in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the summarize_wal setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'summarize_wal'

metrics.rationale: Needed only for native incremental physical backups (PostgreSQL 17 and later). Not required when the declared RPO is 24 hours (as for BAK-1.1); it still earns or loses its points.

metrics.description: Whether full-page-image compression is on (boolean pre-15; lz4/zstd from 15). Cuts WAL volume — smaller archives, faster replication — at modest CPU cost.
metrics.remediation: Set wal_compression=lz4 (PG 15+) or on (PG 14).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the wal_compression setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'wal_compression'

metrics.display_name: Archive Timeout Bounds the Declared RPO
metrics.description: archive_timeout in seconds: how long PostgreSQL may keep changes in the current WAL segment before it forces a switch so the segment can be archived. 0, the default, never forces a switch, so on a quiet database recent changes can wait unarchived for hours. Target-aware: with archiving on, no standby streaming (streaming_status or ha_standby_count) and an RPO of 4 hours or less declared, it must be at least 1 second and no longer than the declared RPO; otherwise any value passes. When neither standby signal was collected, the bands still apply to this advisory metric, while rule PG-CR-RPO-3 stays silent and leaves the declaration its points.
metrics.remediation: Set archive_timeout to at most the declared RPO in seconds (for example 60 for a 5-minute RPO), or connect a streaming standby. Very low values add one mostly empty 16 MB segment per switch to the archive.
metrics.rationale: With continuous archiving the data at risk is the WAL segment not yet archived, and a segment is archived only once it is full or archive_timeout forces a switch. A busy database fills segments within seconds; a quiet one with archive_timeout at 0 can hold a few writes for hours, which breaks a short declared RPO while every archiving check passes. A connected standby (streaming_status true or ha_standby_count at least 1, the same test as PER-4.1) receives WAL continuously, so the setting stops bounding the loss window and the RPO bands are ignored. A daily RPO, or no declaration, is already covered by the 24-hour base-backup freshness bound of BAK-2.2, so any value passes there. Rule PG-CR-RPO-3 links the setting to aggressive RPO declarations.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'archive_timeout'

metrics.description: Whether a documented and recurring backup schedule exists. Without one, recoverability depends on ad-hoc operator action.
metrics.remediation: Document and implement a backup schedule (daily recommended)

metrics.description: Age of the most recent successful base backup. It measures base-backup freshness, not the recoverable point: with continuous WAL archiving a base backup plus the archived WAL recovers up to the last archived WAL segment, so the declared RPO is then judged by the archiving checks instead. How recent that segment is depends on write volume and archive_timeout, which BAK-1.7 and rule PG-CR-RPO-3 judge against the declared RPO once the checker collects archive_timeout. Target-aware (v1.11.0): without WAL archiving the ceiling derives from the declared rpo_target (a declared 1-day RPO makes an 8-hour-old backup completely fine); with archive_mode on or always, or with nothing declared, the 24-hour freshness bound applies.
metrics.remediation: Verify backup jobs are running and completing successfully
metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL recovers from a base backup plus archived WAL (continuous archiving and point-in-time recovery), so when archiving is on the data-loss window is set by the WAL chain, not by the backup age: archive failures (BAK-1.3) and the rule that invalidates an aggressive RPO without WAL transport assess it. Without archiving the last backup is the recovery point and must be as fresh as the declared RPO. A fresh base backup with a failing WAL chain still fails BAK-1.3. On a low-write database the last archived segment can be older than a short declared RPO when archive_timeout is 0 or too long: BAK-1.7 bounds archive_timeout by the declared RPO when no standby is streaming, and PG-CR-RPO-3 invalidates a 5- or 15-minute RPO declaration it cannot meet. Both judge only a collected archive_timeout: until the collector sends it, the gap remains and BAK-1.7 is reported as not provided.

metrics.description: Whether backups are periodically verified for integrity. Untested backups can fail silently until restore time.
metrics.remediation: Implement backup verification process (restore tests)

metrics.description: Whether a purpose-built backup tool (pgBackRest, Barman, pg_probackup, WAL-G) is in use. Hand-rolled scripts lack retention, integrity checks, and incremental support.
metrics.remediation: Consider implementing pgBackRest or Barman for enterprise backup
metrics.rationale: Not required when the declared RPO is 24 hours and the declared RTO is 8 or 24 hours: a daily dump or a full physical backup fits those targets. It still earns or loses its points; undeclared estates are required to meet it.

metrics.description: Whether point-in-time recovery is in place and exercised. Without tested PITR, recovery to a specific moment is not assured.
metrics.remediation: Enable WAL archiving and test PITR procedures
metrics.rationale: Not required when the declared RPO is 24 hours and the declared RTO is 8 or 24 hours: a daily dump or a full physical backup fits those targets. It still earns or loses its points; undeclared estates are required to meet it.

metrics.description: Whether backup artifacts are encrypted at rest. Unencrypted backups expose data if storage is compromised.
metrics.remediation: Enable backup encryption in pgBackRest or use encrypted storage
metrics.rationale: Required above the baseline security posture (hardened, regulated) and on undeclared estates; not required when security_posture=baseline is declared, where it still earns or loses its points.

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Point Objective is documented. Without an RPO, the acceptable data-loss window is undefined.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RPO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a Recovery Time Objective is documented. Without an RTO, recovery duration cannot be measured against a target.
metrics.remediation: Define and document RTO target based on business requirements

metrics.description: Whether a full restore has been exercised within the last 90 days. Untested procedures often fail under real recovery pressure.
metrics.remediation: Schedule regular restore tests (at least quarterly)

metrics.description: Whether a disaster recovery plan exists in writing. Without one, recovery decisions are improvised under stress.
metrics.remediation: Document disaster recovery procedures and runbooks

metrics.description: Streaming replica connection status. A disconnected or unhealthy replica leaves no warm copy for failover.
metrics.remediation: Check replica connectivity and PostgreSQL logs
metrics.rationale: Not required when ha_topology=none is declared: a standalone instance is held to its recovery time by the restore-time rules instead (PG-CR-RTO-3 and PG-CR-RTO-4, which cover recovery times up to 60 minutes, and BAK-4.9). A connected standby still earns its points; undeclared estates are required to have one.

metrics.description: Synchronous replication state capture (sync/async/on/off). Load-bearing input for cross-metric rules; scored loosely — the durability check is PER-4.2 combined with rule PG-CR-SYNC-1.
metrics.remediation: Configure synchronous_commit based on durability requirements

metrics.description: Whether backup retention satisfies the organizational policy. Short retention can violate compliance and limit recovery windows.
metrics.remediation: Configure backup retention to meet compliance requirements

metrics.description: Whether a copy of backups exists at a second location (3-2-1 rule). Single-site backups share fate with the primary during site-level incidents.
metrics.remediation: Replicate backups to a second site or cloud target; verify the copy is restorable independently.

metrics.description: Share of active client connections using SSL, measured over TCP connections; local Unix-socket connections are excluded (collector contract). Cleartext sessions expose credentials and data on the wire.
metrics.remediation: Configure pg_hba.conf to require SSL (hostssl entries only)

metrics.description: Password hashing algorithm (password_encryption). scram-sha-256 is required; md5 is deprecated and weak.
metrics.remediation: Set password_encryption = scram-sha-256 in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'password_encryption'

metrics.description: Count of superuser connections originating from remote hosts. Remote superuser access broadens the attack surface.
metrics.remediation: Restrict superuser to local connections only in pg_hba.conf

metrics.description: Volume of failed authentication attempts over 24 hours. Spikes can indicate brute-force activity or misconfigured clients.
metrics.remediation: Investigate failed login sources and implement rate limiting

metrics.description: Maximum password age in force (e.g. VALID UNTIL or policy tooling). Above 90 days, stale credentials accumulate over time.
metrics.remediation: Implement a password expiration policy using VALID UNTIL

metrics.description: Count of pg_hba.conf entries using md5 authentication. md5 is deprecated; scram-sha-256 should be used instead.
metrics.remediation: Replace MD5 entries with scram-sha-256 in pg_hba.conf

metrics.description: Whether server-side SSL (ssl) is on. Without it, no client connection can be encrypted in transit.
metrics.remediation: Enable SSL: ssl = on in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'ssl'

metrics.description: Minimum TLS protocol version accepted (ssl_min_protocol_version). TLS 1.0/1.1 are deprecated and weak.
metrics.remediation: Set ssl_min_protocol_version = TLSv1.2 in postgresql.conf

metrics.description: Days remaining until the SSL certificate expires. An expired cert breaks all SSL client connections.
metrics.remediation: Renew SSL certificate before expiration

metrics.description: Whether database storage is encrypted at rest (TDE or filesystem/disk encryption). Unencrypted media can leak data if removed or stolen.
metrics.remediation: Implement disk-level encryption or use encrypted tablespaces
metrics.rationale: Required above the baseline security posture (hardened, regulated) and on undeclared estates; not required when security_posture=baseline is declared, where it still earns or loses its points.

metrics.description: Whether data page checksums (data_checksums) are on. Without them, on-disk corruption can go undetected.
metrics.remediation: Reinitialize cluster with --data-checksums or use pg_checksums

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'data_checksums'

metrics.description: Whether connection events are logged (log_connections). Required for auditing who connects and from where.
metrics.remediation: Set log_connections = on in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_connections'

metrics.description: Whether disconnection events are logged (log_disconnections). Useful for session-duration auditing and forensic timelines.
metrics.remediation: Set log_disconnections = on in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the log_disconnections setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_disconnections'

metrics.description: Statement-class logging level (log_statement). A setting of ddl, mod, or all is required to track schema and data changes for audit.
metrics.remediation: Set log_statement = ddl (or mod/all) in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'log_statement'

metrics.description: Whether the pgaudit extension is installed. Required for fine-grained, compliance-grade auditing beyond log_statement. Required when the estate declares a regulated security posture or declares none; at baseline or hardened it counts but is not required.
metrics.remediation: Install and configure the pgaudit extension (shared_preload_libraries, then CREATE EXTENSION pgaudit) and define the audit classes the regulation requires.

technical_anchor.summary: Checks whether pgaudit is installed in the current database.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT count(*) > 0 AS pgaudit_installed FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'pgaudit'

metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL Technology Leader review (2026-09-03): an external extension is required only when it has to be. Required under a regulated posture and on undeclared estates; at baseline or hardened it counts but is not required. PG-CR-SECPOST-2 keeps linking the regulated declaration to the evidence.

metrics.description: Number of days of database logs retained. Short retention can violate compliance and limit incident investigation.
metrics.remediation: Configure log rotation to retain logs for compliance period

metrics.description: Presence of overly permissive grants to the PUBLIC role. Public grants give every user access by default.
metrics.remediation: Revoke unnecessary privileges from PUBLIC role

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) as grant_count
FROM information_schema.role_table_grants
WHERE grantee = 'PUBLIC'
  AND table_schema NOT IN ('pg_catalog', 'information_schema')

metrics.description: Number of roles with the superuser attribute. Excess superusers expand the blast radius if any account is compromised.
metrics.remediation: Reduce superuser accounts to minimum necessary

metrics.description: Whether role inheritance is used to manage privileges. Direct grants on each user scale poorly and obscure the access model.
metrics.remediation: Implement role-based access control with proper inheritance

metrics.description: Whether row-level security policies are applied where data segregation is required. Useful for multi-tenant or sensitive datasets.
metrics.remediation: Consider implementing RLS for multi-tenant or sensitive data

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) as policy_count
FROM pg_policies

metrics.description: Whether ALTER SYSTEM is disabled (allow_alter_system=off). Locking it prevents runtime config drift via SQL.
metrics.remediation: Set allow_alter_system = off in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the allow_alter_system setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'allow_alter_system'

metrics.description: Total database size in GB, captured as an input for target coherence: the restore-time estimate against the declared RTO (BAK-4.9) and the size-weighted bloat measure. Size is never penalised by itself; the storage risk lives in disk_usage_pct (CAP-1.7).
metrics.remediation: Informational capture. When the size makes a declared target unachievable (for example a 15-minute RTO on a standalone instance holding a terabyte), the coherence rules say so; the remedies are an HA topology or a smaller instance.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the size of the current database in GB.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT round(pg_database_size(current_database()) / 1073741824.0, 2) AS database_size_gb

metrics.rationale: Size is not a health signal (the reviewer asked to drop it) but many declared targets depend on it: an RTO of 15 minutes cannot be met by restoring a terabyte on a standalone instance, however good the backups are. Kept as a coherence input (Adrien, 2026-09-03).

metrics.description: Projected days until storage is full given current growth. Fewer than 90 days of runway leaves no time to provision more space. Target-aware (v1.11.0): a tighter declared growth_headroom_target raises the required runway (months_3=90, months_6=180, months_12=365 days); undeclared estates keep the 90-day floor.
metrics.remediation: Plan capacity expansion or implement data lifecycle management

metrics.description: Per-tablespace utilization. A single tablespace running out of space stops writes to objects placed there.
metrics.remediation: Add space to constrained tablespaces

metrics.description: Total partitioned-relation count. Excessive partitions slow planning, autovacuum, and catalog operations.
metrics.remediation: Review partitioning strategy to reduce total partition count

metrics.description: Active connections relative to max_connections. Hitting the cap rejects new sessions including admin logins.
metrics.remediation: Increase max_connections or implement connection pooling

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_connections') as max_conn,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity) as current_conn,
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'superuser_reserved_connections') as reserved

metrics.description: Whether a connection pooler (PgBouncer, Pgpool-II) sits in front of PostgreSQL. Without one, each client process consumes a backend.
metrics.remediation: Implement PgBouncer or Pgpool-II for connection pooling

metrics.description: Share of connections in idle state, assessed only where no connection pooler is declared: on pooled instances a high idle share is expected and benign (warm server connections), while on unpooled instances it signals leaked or unmanaged application connections. The pooled-side signal is PER-3.4 (idle-in-transaction timeout).
metrics.remediation: Configure connection timeouts or review application connection handling

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE state = 'idle') as idle_count,
  COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE backend_type = 'client backend') as total_clients
FROM pg_stat_activity

metrics.description: Whether reserved_connections is non-zero. Reserves slots for non-superuser admin roles when max_connections is saturated.
metrics.remediation: Set reserved_connections > 0 for emergency administrative access

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the reserved_connections setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'reserved_connections'

metrics.description: Whether autovacuum is on. Required to reclaim dead tuples and prevent transaction ID wraparound.
metrics.remediation: Enable autovacuum: autovacuum = on in postgresql.conf

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the autovacuum setting from pg_settings; the value must be on.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'autovacuum'

metrics.rationale: The metric is the autovacuum switch itself (PostgreSQL documentation, Routine Vacuuming); overdue-table analysis belongs to findings, not to this critical. REGRESSIONS R-002: the collector emitted prose here.

metrics.description: Table bloat as dead space weighted by table size across all user tables (dead tuple bytes over total relation bytes), so a few small tables cannot dominate the figure. High bloat wastes storage, slows scans, and signals autovacuum tuning gaps. High-churn OLTP workloads naturally bloat more between vacuums than read-heavy or analytical ones.
metrics.remediation: Run VACUUM FULL on bloated tables or use pg_repack

technical_anchor.summary: Estimates size-weighted dead space from pg_stat_user_tables and the relation sizes.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT round(100.0 * sum(n_dead_tup::numeric * pg_relation_size(relid) / greatest(n_live_tup + n_dead_tup, 1)) / greatest(sum(pg_relation_size(relid)), 1), 1) AS bloat_pct
FROM pg_stat_user_tables

metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL Technology Leader review (2026-09-03): the previous average over the twenty worst tables with more than a thousand rows rested on arbitrary filters; a size-weighted measure needs none.

metrics.description: Average index bloat percentage. Bloated indexes inflate storage and degrade lookup performance.
metrics.remediation: Reindex bloated indexes or use pg_repack

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) as unused_count
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes ui
JOIN pg_index i ON ui.indexrelid = i.indexrelid
WHERE ui.idx_scan = 0
  AND NOT i.indisunique
  AND NOT i.indisprimary
  AND pg_relation_size(ui.indexrelid) > 1048576

metrics.description: Ratio of dead to live tuples. Sustained high values indicate autovacuum is not keeping up with churn.
metrics.remediation: Tune autovacuum parameters or run manual VACUUM

metrics.description: Duration of recent vacuum runs. Long-running vacuums may signal cost throttling, lock contention, or oversized tables.
metrics.remediation: Tune autovacuum cost settings or schedule vacuum during low-traffic periods

metrics.display_name: Maintenance Work Mem Sized to RAM
metrics.description: Sizing of maintenance_work_mem relative to host RAM. Low values slow VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, and other maintenance operations; 5% of RAM is a standard starting point.
metrics.remediation: Increase maintenance_work_mem for faster maintenance operations

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the maintenance_work_mem setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'maintenance_work_mem'

metrics.description: Transaction-ID age relative to wraparound. Approaching the limit forces emergency vacuum and can stop writes.
metrics.remediation: Run VACUUM FREEZE or tune autovacuum_freeze_max_age

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  datname,
  age(datfrozenxid) as xid_age,
  round(100.0 * age(datfrozenxid) / 2147483647, 2) as xid_pct
FROM pg_database
WHERE datallowconn = true
ORDER BY age(datfrozenxid) DESC

metrics.description: Whether a written capacity growth projection exists. Without one, expansion lead times catch teams unprepared.
metrics.remediation: Document expected growth and plan capacity accordingly

metrics.description: Whether a written scaling strategy exists (vertical headroom, read replicas, partitioning/sharding path). Without one, growth decisions are improvised under pressure.
metrics.remediation: Document the next two scaling steps for this database and the trigger conditions for each.

metrics.description: Count of replication slots with excessive lag. Stale slots pin WAL forever and can fill the disk.
metrics.remediation: Drop or reactivate stale replication slots to prevent WAL accumulation

metrics.description: Whether idle_replication_slot_timeout is set. Auto-drops abandoned slots so they cannot pin WAL indefinitely.
metrics.remediation: Set idle_replication_slot_timeout to automatically clean up stale slots

metrics.description: Rows landing in default partitions. Significant overflow signals the partitioning scheme is missing required ranges.
metrics.remediation: Create proper partitions for data currently landing in default partition

metrics.description: Buffer cache hit ratio. Low ratios indicate undersized shared_buffers or unselective queries hitting disk; healthy values depend on workload type — OLTP workloads should sit near 99%, OLAP workloads with working sets larger than RAM operate healthily lower.
metrics.remediation: Increase shared_buffers or optimize queries

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  sum(blks_hit) as hits,
  sum(blks_read) as reads,
  CASE WHEN sum(blks_hit) + sum(blks_read) > 0
    THEN round(100.0 * sum(blks_hit) / (sum(blks_hit) + sum(blks_read)), 2)
    ELSE 100
  END as cache_hit_ratio
FROM pg_stat_database
WHERE datname = current_database()

metrics.description: shared_buffers as a share of host RAM. Undersizing pushes hot pages out of cache; above ~40% the double-buffering against the OS page cache and squeezed work_mem do more harm than good (the documentation flags allocations beyond 40% as unlikely to work better).
metrics.remediation: Set shared_buffers to 25% of available RAM

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting, unit FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'shared_buffers'

metrics.description: Whether effective_cache_size reflects available cache. Underestimates push the planner toward needless sequential scans.
metrics.remediation: Set effective_cache_size to 50-75% of available RAM

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the effective_cache_size setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'effective_cache_size'

metrics.description: Ratio of requested (forced) to timed checkpoints. Frequent forced checkpoints signal undersized max_wal_size and add I/O pressure; write-heavy OLTP workloads tolerate a higher ratio than analytical workloads.
metrics.remediation: Increase checkpoint_timeout or max_wal_size to reduce forced checkpoints

metrics.description: Whether I/O timing collection (track_io_timing) is on. Required for EXPLAIN (BUFFERS) and pg_stat_io to attribute I/O cost.
metrics.remediation: Set track_io_timing = on for I/O performance diagnostics

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the track_io_timing setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'track_io_timing'

metrics.description: Async I/O backend (io_method). io_uring and worker leverage parallel I/O; older defaults serialize requests.
metrics.remediation: Configure io_method for optimal async I/O performance

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the io_method setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'io_method'

metrics.description: checkpoint_completion_target value. Low values concentrate checkpoint I/O into bursts and amplify latency spikes; PostgreSQL 14+ ships with a 0.9 default, which is the modern recommendation.
metrics.remediation: Set checkpoint_completion_target = 0.9 for smoother checkpoints

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_completion_target') as completion_target,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_timeout') as timeout,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_wal_size') as max_wal_size

metrics.description: Whether pg_stat_statements is installed. Required to attribute query latency, calls, and I/O across the workload.
metrics.remediation: Install pg_stat_statements: CREATE EXTENSION pg_stat_statements

technical_anchor.query: SELECT 1 FROM pg_extension WHERE extname = 'pg_stat_statements'

metrics.description: Count of slow queries logged in the last hour. Frequent slow queries indicate missing indexes or inefficient plans.
metrics.remediation: Identify and optimize slow queries using pg_stat_statements

metrics.description: Number of queries currently running for over 5 minutes. Long-runners hold locks and block autovacuum.
metrics.remediation: Investigate and optimize long-running queries

technical_anchor.summary: Counts active queries running longer than five minutes in pg_stat_activity.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  pid,
  now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start)::int as duration_secs,
  substring(query, 1, 200) as query_preview,
  usename,
  state,
  wait_event_type
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE (now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start) > make_interval(secs := '5 minutes'::interval)
  AND state != 'idle'
  AND pid != pg_backend_pid()
ORDER BY query_start ASC
LIMIT 20

metrics.description: Whether the top queries (by pg_stat_statements) were reviewed in the last 90 days. Unreviewed workloads accumulate dead weight and silent regressions.
metrics.remediation: Schedule a quarterly top-N query review against pg_stat_statements.

metrics.description: Whether transaction_timeout is set. Caps maximum transaction duration so runaway sessions cannot pin resources indefinitely.
metrics.remediation: Set transaction_timeout to prevent indefinitely running transactions

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the transaction_timeout setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'transaction_timeout'

metrics.description: Whether enable_partition_pruning is on. Required so the planner skips non-matching partitions instead of scanning them.
metrics.remediation: Set enable_partition_pruning = on in postgresql.conf

metrics.description: Sizing of work_mem relative to host RAM. Low values force sorts and hash joins to spill to disk and slow query execution; the appropriate share of RAM depends on workload type and concurrency.
metrics.remediation: work_mem applies per sort or hash node per query, so the budget is a share of RAM divided by the expected concurrent operations (max_connections times the typical nodes per query). Size it from that share (see the band per workload), verify with pg_stat_statements temp_blks_written, and raise it per role or session where one workload needs more.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting::bigint * CASE unit WHEN 'kB' THEN 1 WHEN 'MB' THEN 1024 ELSE 1 END AS work_mem_kb FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'work_mem'

metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL documentation (work_mem is per operation, not per session) and the PG-CR-MEM-1 memory budget rule; the share of RAM per workload comes from dbi field practice, not from a fixed 16 to 64 MB figure.

metrics.description: random_page_cost setting versus storage type. Defaults match HDD; SSD/NVMe should use ~1.1 to favor index scans.
metrics.remediation: Set random_page_cost = 1.1 for SSD storage

technical_anchor.summary: Reads effective_io_concurrency and random_page_cost together; the pair tells whether the planner was told about SSD storage.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  current_setting('effective_io_concurrency')::int AS eio,
  current_setting('random_page_cost')::numeric AS rpc

metrics.display_name: Temp File Usage Bounded by RAM
metrics.description: Volume of temporary files written since the statistics reset, in bytes, sized relative to host RAM. Temp files come from sorts, hashes, materialised CTEs and maintenance work that exceed work_mem; they are legitimate for large analytical queries and only a problem when they are large, frequent and avoidable.
metrics.remediation: Identify the top temp-file writers in pg_stat_statements (temp_blks_written) and fix or rewrite them first; raise work_mem only for the sessions or roles that need it.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the temp bytes written by the current database since the statistics reset.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT temp_bytes FROM pg_stat_database WHERE datname = current_database()

metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL Technology Leader review (2026-09-03): temporary files are not only a work_mem symptom.

metrics.description: Number of sessions waiting on locks. Persistent waits indicate contention from blocking transactions.
metrics.remediation: Investigate blocking queries and optimize transactions

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  COUNT(*) as blocked_count,
  COUNT(DISTINCT blocked.pid) as blocked_pids
FROM pg_catalog.pg_locks blocked
JOIN pg_catalog.pg_locks blocking
  ON blocking.locktype = blocked.locktype
  AND blocking.database IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.database
  AND blocking.relation IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.relation
  AND blocking.page IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.page
  AND blocking.tuple IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.tuple
  AND blocking.virtualxid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.virtualxid
  AND blocking.transactionid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.transactionid
  AND blocking.classid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.classid
  AND blocking.objid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.objid
  AND blocking.objsubid IS NOT DISTINCT FROM blocked.objsubid
  AND blocking.pid != blocked.pid
WHERE NOT blocked.granted

metrics.description: Deadlock occurrences over 24 hours. Occasional deadlocks are normal in concurrent applications and PostgreSQL resolves them automatically; a recurring rate points to inconsistent lock ordering across transactions.
metrics.remediation: Review transaction ordering to prevent deadlocks

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT deadlocks
FROM pg_stat_database
WHERE datname = current_database()

metrics.description: Number of queries currently blocked. Blocked queries reveal active contention and risk cascading slowdowns.
metrics.remediation: Investigate and resolve blocking sessions

metrics.description: idle_in_transaction_session_timeout value. 0 (off) lets abandoned transactions hold locks and pin xmin, blocking vacuum and inflating bloat.
metrics.remediation: Set to the longest legitimate think-time (commonly 5-30 min).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the idle_in_transaction_session_timeout setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'idle_in_transaction_session_timeout'

metrics.description: Replica lag in seconds. Sustained lag widens RPO and risks stale reads on replicas. Critical on replicated instances; applies_when gates it off for standalone primaries (no streaming standby and no declared standby) so they are never penalized for replication they never claimed.
metrics.remediation: Investigate network latency or replica performance

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  client_addr,
  state,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM replay_lag)::int as replay_lag_secs,
  EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM write_lag)::int as write_lag_secs
FROM pg_stat_replication
WHERE state = 'streaming'

metrics.description: Major version in use. The floor tracks latest-minus-two and is refreshed each catalog release (PG 18 is latest as of 2026; PG 13 reached EOL November 2025, PG 14 reaches EOL November 2026). Older majors miss performance, security, and recovery improvements.
metrics.remediation: Plan upgrade to a supported PostgreSQL version

technical_anchor.query: SHOW server_version

metrics.description: Whether the running major is still under community support. Past EOL, no security fixes are released.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade to a supported PostgreSQL version before EOL

metrics.description: Major versions behind the current upstream release. Falling further behind compounds upgrade risk and forfeits new features.
metrics.remediation: Plan upgrade path to reduce version gap

metrics.description: Patch versions behind on the current major. Skipping minor releases leaves known security and bug fixes unapplied.
metrics.remediation: Apply latest minor/patch version for security and bug fixes

metrics.description: Whether an upgrade posture is declared for the next major upgrade. All-pass declaration (v1.11.0): declaring 'no'/'none' is honest and scores full; incoherence is penalised only by the rules (PG-CR-FUT-1 zeroes a claimed plan while >2 majors behind; PG-CR-FUT-2 deducts when there is no plan AND >2 majors behind). Not declaring at all costs nothing: a blank declaration keeps its full points (1.17.0).
metrics.remediation: Create and maintain upgrade planning documentation

metrics.description: Whether installed extensions have been verified against the target upgrade version. Incompatible extensions block upgrades.
metrics.remediation: Test extension compatibility before major upgrades

metrics.description: Use of features marked deprecated in the current major. Deprecated features are removal candidates in future versions.
metrics.remediation: Review and remove usage of deprecated features

metrics.description: Number of roles still using md5-hashed passwords. md5 is deprecated and slated for removal; migrate to scram-sha-256.
metrics.remediation: Migrate all roles from MD5 to SCRAM-SHA-256 authentication

metrics.description: Whether the database reports to an external monitoring system. Without monitoring, anomalies surface only as outages.
metrics.remediation: Connect database to monitoring solution (Zabbix, PMM, Datadog, etc.)

metrics.description: Whether alert rules cover critical health metrics. Without alerts, breaches go unnoticed until escalation.
metrics.remediation: Configure alerts for critical health metrics

metrics.description: Whether database documentation is current. Stale docs delay troubleshooting and onboarding under pressure.
metrics.remediation: Maintain current documentation for database configuration

metrics.description: Number of leader nodes reported by Patroni. Anything other than one indicates split-brain or an election in progress.
metrics.remediation: Investigate split-brain scenario and resolve cluster state

metrics.description: Whether all cluster members share the same WAL timeline. Diverged timelines mean replicas need reinitialization.
metrics.remediation: Reinitialize diverged replicas to rejoin cluster timeline

metrics.description: Whether at least one replica is healthy and caught up enough to be promoted. Without a candidate, leader loss means downtime.
metrics.remediation: Ensure at least one synchronous replica is healthy and caught up

metrics.description: Whether Patroni watchdog fencing is on. Without it, a hung leader cannot be reliably stopped before a replica is promoted.
metrics.remediation: Enable watchdog device and configure Patroni watchdog settings

metrics.description: Activity and lag of Patroni-managed replication slots. Inactive or lagging slots break the failover safety net.
metrics.remediation: Check and clean up inactive replication slots

metrics.description: Validity of Patroni timing parameters (ttl, loop_wait, retry_timeout). Inconsistent values cause spurious failovers or sluggish recovery.
metrics.remediation: Review and adjust Patroni timing parameters for cluster stability

metrics.description: Whether any Patroni member has a pending-restart flag. Pending restarts mean config changes have not yet taken effect.
metrics.remediation: Apply pending restarts during maintenance window

metrics.description: Whether traffic to the DCS (etcd/Consul/ZooKeeper) is encrypted with TLS. Cleartext DCS traffic exposes cluster metadata.
metrics.remediation: Enable TLS for DCS client connections

metrics.description: Whether the Patroni REST API requires credentials. Unauthenticated APIs allow unfettered cluster control.
metrics.remediation: Configure Patroni REST API authentication credentials

metrics.description: Number of Patroni members. Too few members cannot form quorum; loss of one node halts the cluster.
metrics.remediation: Add cluster members to meet minimum quorum requirements

metrics.description: Recent failover count. Frequent failovers signal infrastructure instability or aggressive timing parameters.
metrics.remediation: Investigate root cause of frequent failovers

metrics.description: Patroni release version in use. Old versions miss bug fixes and may interoperate poorly with current PostgreSQL.
metrics.remediation: Upgrade Patroni to latest stable version

metrics.description: Whether the Patroni REST API serves over TLS. Cleartext API exposes credentials and cluster state on the network.
metrics.remediation: Configure TLS certificates for Patroni REST API

metrics.description: Whether Patroni DCS failsafe_mode is on. Lets the cluster keep serving when the DCS is briefly unreachable.
metrics.remediation: Enable failsafe_mode in Patroni configuration

metrics.description: Quality of HNSW indexes (recall, build settings). Poor build parameters degrade vector search accuracy and latency.
metrics.remediation: Rebuild HNSW indexes with tuned ef_construction and m parameters

metrics.description: Dead-tuple ratio on vector tables. Bloat on large vector tables disproportionately slows index scans and rebuilds.
metrics.remediation: Run VACUUM on vector tables and tune autovacuum for large tables

metrics.description: Cache hit ratio on vector index pages. Low hit rates push vector search onto disk and inflate query latency.
metrics.remediation: Increase shared_buffers or reduce index size with quantization

metrics.description: Health of TimescaleDB compression jobs. Failing jobs let storage grow unchecked and waste retention budget.
metrics.remediation: Check and repair failed compression jobs in timescaledb_information.jobs

metrics.description: Hypertable chunk count. Excessive chunks slow planning and catalog operations on time-series workloads.
metrics.remediation: Adjust chunk_time_interval or enable compression to reduce chunk count

metrics.description: Whether TimescaleDB retention policies are defined and running. Without them, data accumulates beyond useful lifetime.
metrics.remediation: Configure retention policies using add_retention_policy()

metrics.description: Number of inactive shard placements in Citus. Inactive placements break query routing and risk data unavailability.
metrics.remediation: Repair or recreate unhealthy shard placements

metrics.description: Reachability of Citus worker nodes. An unreachable worker takes its shards offline for queries.
metrics.remediation: Check network connectivity and worker node health

metrics.description: Whether pg_partman has pre-created partitions ahead of incoming data. Falling behind sends rows into the default partition.
metrics.remediation: Run partman maintenance or increase premake value

metrics.description: The planning horizon for which current storage headroom is expected to suffice (3, 6, or 12 months). Corroborated against observed storage utilization; the declaration itself is never penalized.
metrics.remediation: Declare the growth horizon and ensure current storage utilization leaves room to reach it before capacity is exhausted.

metrics.description: Whether pg_partman retention is defined and active. Without it, old partitions accumulate forever.
metrics.remediation: Configure retention in part_config and run maintenance

metrics.description: Count of pg_cron jobs that failed in the last 24 hours. Failed jobs leave maintenance work undone.
metrics.remediation: Check cron.job_run_details for failed jobs and fix underlying issues

metrics.description: Whether a known backup tool can be inferred from archive_command. Unknown tooling makes recovery procedures harder to validate.
metrics.remediation: Configure a recognized backup tool in archive_command
metrics.rationale: Inferred from archive_command, so it only says something when WAL archiving carries the recovery point. Not required when the declared RPO is 24 hours (as for BAK-1.1); a detected tool still earns its points.

metrics.description: Share of table scans that use indexes rather than sequential scans. Low values point to missing indexes or planner cost misconfiguration.
metrics.remediation: Review and add indexes for frequently scanned tables

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  SUM(idx_scan) as idx_scans,
  SUM(seq_scan) as seq_scans,
  CASE WHEN SUM(idx_scan) + SUM(seq_scan) > 0
    THEN round(100.0 * SUM(idx_scan) / (SUM(idx_scan) + SUM(seq_scan)), 2)
    ELSE 100
  END as idx_hit_ratio
FROM pg_stat_user_tables

metrics.description: Share of scans on large tables that go through sequential scan. Interpreted loosely: sequential scans are the correct plan for small tables and wide-selectivity queries, so the ratio is meaningful only when the collector scopes it to large tables. High scoped ratios suggest missing or unused indexes.
metrics.remediation: Add appropriate indexes for large tables with high sequential scan ratios

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  schemaname || '.' || relname as table_name,
  n_live_tup,
  seq_scan,
  idx_scan,
  CASE WHEN idx_scan > 0
    THEN round(seq_scan::numeric / idx_scan, 1)
    ELSE seq_scan
  END as seq_to_idx_ratio
FROM pg_stat_user_tables
WHERE n_live_tup > 5000
  AND seq_scan > 100
  AND (seq_scan > idx_scan OR seq_scan > idx_scan * 5)
ORDER BY seq_scan DESC
LIMIT 5

metrics.description: Number of streaming standbys connected. Without at least one, leader loss means full outage until recovery.
metrics.remediation: Configure streaming replication with at least one standby for high availability

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) as standby_count
FROM pg_stat_replication
WHERE state = 'streaming'

metrics.rationale: Not required when ha_topology=none is declared: a standalone instance is held to its recovery time by the restore-time rules instead (PG-CR-RTO-3 and PG-CR-RTO-4, which cover recovery times up to 60 minutes, and BAK-4.9). A connected standby still earns its points; undeclared estates are required to have one.

metrics.description: Measured restore throughput from the last restore test, in MB per second. Used to estimate restore time against the declared RTO (BAK-4.9); when not attested the engine assumes the policy default of 200 MB/s.
metrics.remediation: Record the throughput observed during the last restore test (restored bytes divided by elapsed seconds).
metrics.rationale: A declaration, never graded on its value: an estate that tested its restore knows its rate, and that rate decides whether the declared RTO is achievable.

metrics.description: Estimated minutes for the data-restore phase of a full restore from backup: database size divided by the attested restore throughput, or by the policy default of 200 MB/s when no restore test attested a rate. It estimates one phase only: detection, provisioning, WAL replay, validation and application reconnection come on top, and an unattested rate is an assumption, not a measurement. Scored against the declared RTO rung. Required only without a declared HA topology: with a standby or a managed cluster, failover defines the RTO for the loss of an instance, so the estimate still counts but is not required; recovery from logical damage still needs a restore and is not assessed here.
metrics.remediation: Add an HA topology so failover, not a restore, bounds the RTO, or move the large database to a dedicated instance. If the business accepts a longer recovery, the declared rto_target is wrong: correct it; the restore estimate is then judged against the looser recovery time and the declarations code changes.
metrics.rationale: Engine-derived: database_size GB times 1024 divided by the throughput in MB/s divided by 60. The 200 MB/s default is a conservative pgBackRest or barman restore on SSD and lives in the scoring policy. The default is an assumption until restore tests calibrate it; an attested rate (BAK-4.8) replaces it, and an observed recovery exercise is stronger evidence than any estimate.

metrics.description: Number of logins holding azure_pg_admin (the highest privilege on Azure). Excess members enlarge the blast radius if any account is compromised.
metrics.remediation: Limit azure_pg_admin membership to strictly necessary administrative accounts (max 1-2)

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT r.rolname
FROM pg_roles r
JOIN pg_auth_members m ON m.member = r.oid
JOIN pg_roles g ON g.oid = m.roleid
WHERE g.rolname = 'azure_pg_admin'
  AND r.rolcanlogin = true

metrics.description: The declared security posture for this instance (baseline, hardened, or regulated). Declaring it sets the expectation that configuration evidence — encryption, audit logging — corroborates the claim; the declaration itself is never penalized.
metrics.remediation: Declare the security posture matching this instance's compliance scope, then align SSL/TLS and audit logging to it.

metrics.description: PgBouncer pool_mode value. transaction mode maximizes connection reuse; session mode pins backends for the session lifetime.
metrics.remediation: Set pgbouncer.pool_mode = 'transaction' unless application requires session mode (prepared statements, advisory locks)

metrics.description: PgBouncer default_pool_size relative to max_connections. Too small starves workloads; too large defeats pooling.
metrics.remediation: Tune pgbouncer.default_pool_size to 2-3x vCPU count; each user/db pair gets its own pool

metrics.description: PgBouncer max_client_conn ceiling. Too low rejects clients before pooling can absorb the load.
metrics.remediation: Increase pgbouncer.max_client_conn if application needs more concurrent client connections

metrics.description: PgBouncer min_pool_size value. A non-zero floor pre-warms backends to absorb traffic spikes without cold-start latency.
metrics.remediation: Tune pgbouncer.min_pool_size to 1-3 for pre-warmed connections, balancing warmth vs resource usage

metrics.description: Whether PgBouncer ignore_startup_parameters drops critical application settings. Suppressing required parameters can break clients silently.
metrics.remediation: Review pgbouncer.ignore_startup_parameters to ensure application compatibility

metrics.description: Whether the largest tables have been reviewed for abandoned rows and outsized footprints. Unreviewed top tables hide easy wins for storage and bloat.
metrics.remediation: Review large tables for dead rows (VACUUM), abandoned data (DROP), or archival candidates

metrics.description: Filesystem utilization of the volume(s) hosting PGDATA and WAL. Sustained use above 85% risks refusing writes and failed WAL archiving.
metrics.remediation: Extend the volume, prune obsolete WAL/backups, or move tablespaces.

metrics.description: temp_file_limit value (collector maps unlimited to 0). Unlimited lets one pathological sort fill the volume shared with PGDATA.
metrics.remediation: Cap per-process temp usage (e.g. 5-10% of the data volume).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the temp_file_limit setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'temp_file_limit'

metrics.description: Sizing of autovacuum_freeze_max_age. Too low triggers premature anti-wraparound vacuums; above 1.5B it leaves dangerously little headroom before the ~2.1B hard limit.
metrics.remediation: Keep autovacuum_freeze_max_age at default (200M) or higher; lower values trigger more aggressive anti-wraparound vacuum

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'autovacuum_freeze_max_age'

metrics.description: Number of user tables with autovacuum_enabled=false. Disabled tables accumulate bloat and risk wraparound unless vacuumed manually.
metrics.remediation: Re-enable autovacuum: ALTER TABLE <name> SET (autovacuum_enabled = true). If intentionally disabled, schedule manual VACUUM.

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  c.relnamespace::regnamespace || '.' || c.relname as table_name,
  c.reloptions,
  s.n_dead_tup,
  s.n_live_tup,
  pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(c.oid)) as total_size
FROM pg_class c
JOIN pg_stat_user_tables s ON s.relid = c.oid
WHERE c.reloptions::text LIKE '%autovacuum_enabled=false%'
ORDER BY s.n_dead_tup DESC

metrics.description: Number of unused indexes consuming storage. Unused indexes waste space and add write overhead without aiding queries.
metrics.remediation: Review and drop unused indexes to reduce storage and write overhead

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT COUNT(*) as unused_count
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes ui
JOIN pg_index i ON ui.indexrelid = i.indexrelid
WHERE ui.idx_scan = 0
  AND NOT i.indisunique
  AND NOT i.indisprimary

metrics.description: Whether track_counts is on. Autovacuum scheduling depends on it: off means no dead-tuple accounting and no automatic vacuum triggering.
metrics.remediation: Set track_counts=on (the default).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the track_counts setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'track_counts'

metrics.description: autovacuum_max_workers value. Floor check (3 is the shipped default): passing means not-misconfigured, not tuned. More workers share one cost budget, so the real throughput lever is CAP-3.12; raise workers only on wide schemas where tables queue behind long-running vacuums.
metrics.remediation: Raise to 4-6 on many-table databases; rebalance autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit accordingly.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'autovacuum_max_workers'

metrics.rationale: The floor of 3 is the shipped default; passing means not misconfigured. There is no authoritative tables-per-worker ratio: workers share one cost budget, so throughput comes from autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit (CAP-3.12).

metrics.description: Effective autovacuum cost limit (collector resolves -1 inheritance from vacuum_cost_limit). The shipped default 200 predates modern storage; guidance for SSD-era hardware is 1000-4000. If it stays low while workers increase, each worker gets a smaller throttle share and vacuum falls behind.
metrics.remediation: Raise (1000-4000 on SSD) when bloat metrics trend up; the budget is shared across workers.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit'

metrics.description: effective_io_concurrency value relative to storage type, assessed on PG 17 and older where the default 1 serializes I/O on SSD/NVMe. PG 18 changed the parameter's semantics and default (16) under the new async I/O model, which PER-1.6 assesses instead.
metrics.remediation: Set effective_io_concurrency = 200 for SSD/NVMe storage (default 1 severely underestimates modern I/O capability)

technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'effective_io_concurrency'

metrics.rationale: PostgreSQL documentation: values in the hundreds are appropriate for SSD and NVMe storage; the pgtune SSD preset is 200. The threshold of 100 is the floor. No storage-type guard: a missing system fact would drop the metric.

metrics.description: log_min_duration_statement threshold. -1 disables slow-query logging; very high values miss real outliers.
metrics.remediation: Set log_min_duration_statement = 1000 (1s) to capture slow queries in logs; -1 disables (not recommended)

technical_anchor.query: SELECT current_setting('log_min_duration_statement') AS val

metrics.description: Slots remaining in max_worker_processes after background workers. Too few slots starve parallel query plans.
metrics.remediation: Increase max_worker_processes to ensure enough slots for parallel queries (requires restart). Azure uses 4-6 slots internally.

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_worker_processes') AS max_workers,
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_parallel_workers') AS max_parallel,
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_parallel_workers_per_gather') AS max_per_gather,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'background worker') AS active_bg_workers

metrics.description: max_parallel_workers relative to CPU count — at least half the cores should be available to parallel query. The flat default (8) undersizes large hosts.
metrics.remediation: Set max_parallel_workers = CPU/vCPU count (e.g., 8 for an 8-core system)

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_worker_processes') AS max_workers,
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_parallel_workers') AS max_parallel,
  (SELECT setting::int FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_parallel_workers_per_gather') AS max_per_gather,
  (SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE backend_type = 'background worker') AS active_bg_workers

metrics.description: max_parallel_workers_per_gather value. Zero disables intra-query parallelism; very low values limit per-query speedup. Pure-OLTP shops legitimately disable per-gather parallelism, so under the oltp profile this is capture-only.
metrics.remediation: Set max_parallel_workers_per_gather = CPU_count / 2 for balanced parallelism

metrics.description: Whether background-worker slot allocation has been reviewed. Useful on managed services where the platform consumes hidden slots.
metrics.remediation: Review background worker allocation to identify resource consumers; managed services run internal workers that count against the budget.

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT application_name, count(*) as cnt
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE backend_type = 'background worker'
GROUP BY application_name
ORDER BY application_name

metrics.description: Capture mode of Azure Query Store (pg_qs.query_capture_mode). 'none' disables performance analytics on the platform.
metrics.remediation: Set pg_qs.query_capture_mode = 'top' in Azure Portal to enable query performance analytics

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the Azure query store mode parameter.
technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  current_setting('pg_qs.query_capture_mode', true) AS qs_mode,
  current_setting('pg_qs.retention_period_in_days', true) AS qs_retention,
  current_setting('pgms_wait_sampling.query_capture_mode', true) AS ws_mode,
  current_setting('pgms_wait_sampling.history_period', true) AS ws_period

metrics.description: Capture mode of Azure wait-event sampling (pgms_wait_sampling.query_capture_mode). Required to attribute waits to specific queries.
metrics.remediation: Set pgms_wait_sampling.query_capture_mode = 'all' to analyze what queries are waiting on (I/O, locks, latches)

metrics.description: Azure Intelligent Tuning feature status. Captured for context and scored loosely.
metrics.remediation: Enable Azure intelligent tuning for automated parameter tuning recommendations

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the Azure intelligent tuning parameter.
technical_anchor.query: SELECT current_setting('intelligent_tuning.metric_targets', true) AS metric_targets

metrics.description: checkpoint_timeout value. The shipped default 300s forces frequent checkpoints under production write load; tuning guidance is 15-30 minutes, trading longer crash recovery for less WAL churn. Advisory because 300s remains a defensible deliberate choice on read-mostly instances.
metrics.remediation: Set checkpoint_timeout to 15-30 minutes (900-1800s) on write-active production instances; keep an eye on recovery-time expectations when raising it

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_completion_target') as completion_target,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_timeout') as timeout,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_wal_size') as max_wal_size

metrics.description: max_wal_size value. Floor check (1 GB is the shipped default): passing means not-misconfigured, not tuned; busy writers need several GB. Undersizing forces frequent forced checkpoints and increases write amplification.
metrics.remediation: Increase max_wal_size to at least 1GB (2GB for large databases) to reduce checkpoint overhead

technical_anchor.query:
SELECT
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_completion_target') as completion_target,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'checkpoint_timeout') as timeout,
  (SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_wal_size') as max_wal_size

metrics.description: Whether the azure.extensions allowlist contains the extensions the workload needs. CREATE EXTENSION fails for any extension absent from the list.
metrics.remediation: Keep the azure.extensions allowlist aligned with the extensions the workload actually uses, nothing more; an allow-listed extension does not need to be installed.

technical_anchor.query: SELECT current_setting('azure.extensions', true) AS allowlist

metrics.description: Whether fsync is on. fsync=off abandons crash safety entirely — an OS crash or power loss can corrupt the cluster beyond recovery.
metrics.remediation: Set fsync=on. If write latency forced it off, fix storage instead (BBU cache, NVMe) — never run production with fsync=off.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the fsync setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'fsync'

metrics.description: Whether full_page_writes is on. When off, torn pages after a crash are unrecoverable unless the filesystem guarantees atomic 8 kB writes (e.g. ZFS).
metrics.remediation: Set full_page_writes=on unless the storage stack provably prevents torn pages.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the full_page_writes setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'full_page_writes'

metrics.description: min_wal_size value. Too small recycles WAL segments aggressively and re-creates them under load spikes.
metrics.remediation: Raise min_wal_size (commonly 1-2 GB on busy systems) so recycling absorbs bursts.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the min_wal_size setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'min_wal_size'

metrics.description: Whether PostgreSQL is configured to use Linux huge pages for shared memory. With shared_buffers in the multi-GB range, 4 KB pages multiply TLB misses; huge pages (2 MB) reduce them.
metrics.remediation: Set huge_pages=try (recommended) or huge_pages=on; ensure vm.nr_hugepages is sized to shared_buffers / 2 MB on the host.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the huge_pages setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'huge_pages'

metrics.description: Number of huge pages reserved by the OS (vm.nr_hugepages). When huge_pages=on but the kernel has no pages allocated, PostgreSQL refuses to start; with huge_pages=try it silently falls back to 4 KB pages and the parameter setting is misleading.
metrics.remediation: Reserve huge pages on the host: set vm.nr_hugepages = (shared_buffers / 2 MB) in /etc/sysctl.conf and apply.

metrics.description: Configuration heuristic, not a bound: shared_buffers plus max_connections × work_mem as a share of host RAM. work_mem applies per sort or hash operation, a query can run several at once and hash operations may use hash_mem_multiplier times work_mem, so real peak use can be higher, while most connections use far less. Beyond ~80% the configuration leaves little room for the OS page cache. Measured memory pressure (swap, OOM events) is a separate question. Derived by the engine from shared_buffers_bytes, max_connections, work_mem_bytes, and systemFacts.ram_bytes.
metrics.remediation: Reduce shared_buffers, lower max_connections (use a pooler), or shrink work_mem. Target 60-75% of RAM as the reserved budget so the OS page cache retains room.
metrics.rationale: The formula reads configuration only. PostgreSQL documents work_mem as a per-operation limit and hash_mem_multiplier as a multiplier for hash operations, so the sum is neither a worst case nor an average; it flags configurations where a normal concurrent load can plausibly exhaust RAM. It is not tuned to make any chosen estate score 100.

metrics.description: Size of the WAL buffers in bytes. PostgreSQL auto-tunes to 1/32 of shared_buffers capped at 16 MB; values below 8 MB indicate an explicit throttling misconfiguration that causes WALWrite waits under commit load.
metrics.remediation: Leave wal_buffers at -1 (auto-tuned to 3% of shared_buffers, capped at 16 MB) or set explicitly to 16 MB on busy systems.

metrics.description: Raw shared_buffers value in bytes — the load-bearing input for memory-budget and huge-pages relation rules. Scored loosely (only the relation rules and derived metrics consume it); the percent-of-RAM healthiness check lives in PER-1.2.
metrics.remediation: Set shared_buffers to at least 128 MB; for production workloads target 25 % of RAM (see PER-1.2).

metrics.description: JIT compilation state capture. Scored loosely — enforcement lives in rule PG-CR-OLAP-JIT-1 (jit off under an OLAP profile); jit=off is a legitimate OLTP latency tuning, and PG 19 turns JIT off by default.
metrics.remediation: Match JIT to the workload: enable it for analytical (OLAP) query mixes, keep it off for latency-sensitive OLTP (PG 19 turns it off by default); tune jit_above_cost and jit_inline_above_cost when enabled.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the jit setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'jit'

metrics.description: ANALYZE sample-size knob. The default of 100 is fine for OLTP but underfits analytical queries on wide tables, where planner row estimates drift and join orders go bad. OLAP profiles benefit from 500-1000.
metrics.remediation: OLTP: keep default_statistics_target at 100. OLAP / mixed-with-analytical: raise to 500 or 1000 globally, then ANALYZE.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the default_statistics_target setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'default_statistics_target'

metrics.description: Raw work_mem value in bytes — load-bearing input for the memory-pressure budget rule. Scored loosely; the percent-of-RAM healthiness check (workload-profile-keyed) lives in PER-2.7.
metrics.remediation: Set work_mem to at least 4 MB; tune per workload (see PER-2.7 for size-relative guidance).

metrics.description: Configured upper bound on concurrent backends. Load-bearing input for the memory-budget derived metric — high max_connections × work_mem multiplies into significant reserved memory. The utilization/headroom check lives in CAP-2.1.
metrics.remediation: Right-size max_connections to (peak_concurrent_app_conns + headroom); use a connection pooler instead of raising the cap above 200-400.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the max_connections setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'max_connections'

metrics.description: statement_timeout value at cluster or role level. 0 means a runaway query can hold resources indefinitely.
metrics.remediation: Set a server-wide ceiling (e.g. 5 min) and tighter per-role limits for application users.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the statement_timeout setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'statement_timeout'

metrics.description: Durability tier for COMMIT. Modes off/local return before any standby acknowledgement; remote_write/remote_apply/on require at least one synchronous standby to acknowledge. Declaring synchronous_standby_names while running with off/local silently undermines the advertised durability — caught by the SYNC consistency rule.
