metrics.remediation: Pick a synchronous_commit tier that matches your declared durability: remote_apply (strongest), remote_write (stronger), on (default), local (async to standbys), off (no fsync guarantee).

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the synchronous_commit setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'synchronous_commit'

metrics.description: Count of standby names declared in synchronous_standby_names. Derived by the engine from the raw CSV setting. Used by the SYNC consistency rule to detect 'synchronous_commit weakened while sync standbys are declared'.
metrics.remediation: If you intend synchronous replication, declare standbys in synchronous_standby_names AND set synchronous_commit to on/remote_write/remote_apply.

metrics.description: Raw comma-separated synchronous_standby_names setting. Powers the synchronous_standby_names_count derived metric; the actual durability check is PER-4.2 (synchronous_commit mode) combined with the SYNC consistency rule.
metrics.remediation: Leave empty for asynchronous-only replication, or list standby application_name values for synchronous replication.

technical_anchor.summary: Reads the synchronous_standby_names setting from pg_settings
technical_anchor.query: SELECT setting FROM pg_settings WHERE name = 'synchronous_standby_names'

metrics.rationale: An empty setting is correct for asynchronous-only replication. Not required under a declared ha_topology=none or async_standby; a missing advisory value costs nothing either way.

metrics.description: Count of logical-replication subscriptions disabled or in error (pg_stat_subscription / pg_subscription). A stalled subscription silently diverges the target and pins WAL via its slot.
metrics.remediation: Investigate worker errors (conflicts, missing tables), re-enable, and monitor slot lag.

metrics.description: The declared high-availability topology (none, async standby, sync standby, or cluster-managed). Corroborated against replication configuration and streaming status; the declaration itself is never penalized.
metrics.remediation: Declare the HA topology in place and align streaming / synchronous replication configuration to it.

consistency_rules.title: Backup schedule cannot meet requested RPO
consistency_rules.description: rpo_5/rpo_15 require continuous WAL archiving or streaming replication; daily dumps alone cannot achieve sub-hour RPO.

on_violation.title: RPO target unachievable with declared backup schedule
on_violation.description: rpo_target={value:rpo_target} but dump_schedule={value:dump_schedule}; backup-only RPO is bounded by the dump interval.
on_violation.remediation: Switch dump_schedule to continuous/wal_only or add streaming replication so backups meet the declared RPO. If the business truly accepts a 24-hour recovery point, the declared rpo_target is wrong: correct it to rpo_1440, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Archive mode enabled without a real archive command
consistency_rules.description: archive_mode is on/always but archive_command is empty or a placeholder — WAL is never actually archived.

on_violation.title: WAL archiving is enabled but archive_command is a no-op
on_violation.description: archive_mode={value:archive_mode} with archive_command={value:archive_command}; WAL segments are not being persisted off-server.
on_violation.remediation: Set archive_command to a real script that copies WAL to durable storage (or to your backup tool's archive helper).

consistency_rules.title: PITR claimed but wal_level too low
consistency_rules.description: Point-in-time recovery requires wal_level=replica or logical; wal_level=minimal cannot support PITR.

on_violation.title: PITR enabled but wal_level=minimal cannot support it
on_violation.description: pitr_enabled={value:pitr_enabled} with wal_level={value:wal_level}; PITR will not work until wal_level is raised to replica or logical.
on_violation.remediation: Set wal_level=replica (or logical) in postgresql.conf and restart the server.

consistency_rules.title: SSL enabled but most connections are not using it
consistency_rules.description: SSL is configured server-side but a non-trivial share of clients are still connecting in cleartext.

on_violation.title: SSL is enabled but not enforced — only {value:ssl_connection_pct}% of connections are using SSL
on_violation.description: ssl_enabled=on but ssl_connection_pct={value:ssl_connection_pct}; clients can still negotiate cleartext connections.
on_violation.remediation: Require SSL in pg_hba.conf (hostssl entries only) and reject host entries; ensure all client connection strings use sslmode=require or stricter.

consistency_rules.title: Memory pressure compounded by huge_pages=off
consistency_rules.description: Reserved PostgreSQL memory is past the safe headroom AND the kernel is serving it with 4 KB pages. TLB pressure and page-cache contention are both elevated.

on_violation.title: Memory budget tight with huge_pages=off
on_violation.description: memory_pressure_pct={value:memory_pressure_pct}% with huge_pages={value:huge_pages}; TLB misses and OS-cache contention compound the budget pressure.
on_violation.remediation: Either reduce shared_buffers, lower max_connections × work_mem, or enable huge_pages=try with vm.nr_hugepages = shared_buffers / 2 MB.

consistency_rules.title: Huge pages disabled on a large shared_buffers configuration
consistency_rules.description: shared_buffers in the multi-GB range is served with 4 KB pages — TLB pressure measurably degrades throughput. Set huge_pages=try and reserve vm.nr_hugepages.

on_violation.title: shared_buffers ≥ 8 GB with huge_pages=off
on_violation.description: shared_buffers_bytes={value:shared_buffers_bytes} but huge_pages={value:huge_pages}; the buffer pool is served with 4 KB pages.
on_violation.remediation: Set huge_pages=try and reserve vm.nr_hugepages = shared_buffers / 2 MB on the host, then restart PostgreSQL.

consistency_rules.title: SSD-tuned cost but effective_io_concurrency low
consistency_rules.description: random_page_cost is set as if storage were SSD (≤ 2), but effective_io_concurrency is left at default — the planner expects parallel I/O the executor never issues.

on_violation.title: SSD planner cost without matching IO concurrency
on_violation.description: random_page_cost={value:random_page_cost} (SSD-tuned) with effective_io_concurrency={value:effective_io_concurrency}; the planner expects parallel I/O that the executor will serialize.
on_violation.remediation: Set effective_io_concurrency to 200 (SSD) or 256+ (NVMe). Leave random_page_cost at 1.1-1.5 for SSD storage.

consistency_rules.title: OLAP workload with JIT disabled
consistency_rules.description: Workload profile is declared OLAP but jit=off. Long-running analytical queries lose JIT's expression-compilation speedup (often 10-30%).

on_violation.title: OLAP profile declared but jit={value:jit}
on_violation.description: Workload profile is OLAP but JIT compilation is off. Analytical queries miss JIT's expression-compilation speedup.
on_violation.remediation: Enable JIT for this analytical workload (jit=on; note PG 19 turns it off by default, so set it explicitly). Tune jit_above_cost / jit_inline_above_cost to the query mix.

consistency_rules.title: Synchronous standbys declared but commit semantics undermine them
consistency_rules.description: synchronous_standby_names lists at least one standby but synchronous_commit is set to off or local — commits return before any standby acknowledges. The declared durability is fiction.

on_violation.title: synchronous_commit={value:synchronous_commit} with {value:synchronous_standby_names_count} sync standby(s) declared
on_violation.description: synchronous_standby_names is populated but synchronous_commit={value:synchronous_commit}; the cluster commits before any standby acknowledges and the advertised durability tier is not actually enforced.
on_violation.remediation: Match commit semantics to the declared topology: set synchronous_commit=remote_apply (strongest), remote_write, or on. Pick the tier that matches your RPO target.

consistency_rules.title: Hourly backups cannot meet a 5-minute RPO
consistency_rules.description: rpo_5 requires continuous WAL archiving or synchronous replication; hourly dumps bound the achievable RPO at one hour.

on_violation.title: RPO target unachievable with hourly backups
on_violation.description: rpo_target={value:rpo_target} but dump_schedule={value:dump_schedule}; backup-only RPO is bounded by the dump interval.
on_violation.remediation: Switch dump_schedule to continuous/wal_only so backups meet the declared 5-minute RPO. If the business truly accepts an hour of data loss, the declared rpo_target is wrong: correct it to rpo_60, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: huge_pages=on but no OS huge pages allocated
consistency_rules.description: huge_pages=on is a hard requirement: without reserved OS huge pages, PostgreSQL refuses to start. The misconfiguration is invisible until the next restart.

on_violation.title: PostgreSQL will fail to start on next restart
on_violation.description: huge_pages=on with no allocated OS huge pages: the next restart cannot map shared memory and the instance stays down.
on_violation.remediation: Set vm.nr_hugepages to cover shared_buffers (plus ~10%), or use huge_pages=try.

consistency_rules.title: Autovacuum enabled but track_counts is off
consistency_rules.description: Autovacuum scheduling depends on the statistics collector: with track_counts off there is no dead-tuple accounting and autovacuum never triggers, even though it appears enabled.

on_violation.title: Autovacuum is blind: track_counts=off stops dead-tuple accounting
on_violation.description: track_counts=off silently disables autovacuum triggering — bloat and wraparound risk accumulate unnoticed.
on_violation.remediation: Set track_counts=on (the default) and investigate why it was disabled.

consistency_rules.title: High max_connections with no connection pooler
consistency_rules.description: Each backend is an OS process; beyond ~500 direct connections, memory (multiplied by work_mem) and scheduler pressure grow faster than throughput.

on_violation.title: max_connections={value:max_connections} with no pooler
on_violation.description: A pooler absorbs connection churn at a fraction of the per-backend cost and lets max_connections drop to a sane bound.
on_violation.remediation: Deploy PgBouncer or Pgpool-II in transaction mode and lower max_connections.

consistency_rules.title: No data checksums and restores never tested
consistency_rules.description: Without page checksums, on-disk corruption is invisible; without restore drills, corrupted backups are discovered only at recovery time.

on_violation.title: Silent corruption could propagate into untested backups
on_violation.description: Page-level corruption can flow into every backup generation unnoticed and surface only during a real recovery.
on_violation.remediation: Enable checksums at the next rebuild (or via pg_checksums offline) and schedule quarterly restore tests.

consistency_rules.title: Aggressive RPO declared without WAL archiving or streaming replication
consistency_rules.description: rpo_5/rpo_15 require continuous WAL shipping. With archive_mode=off and no streaming standby connected, the declared RPO has no technical basis.

on_violation.title: Declared RPO {value:rpo_target} is unachievable — no WAL archiving or replication
on_violation.description: rpo_target={value:rpo_target} but archive_mode={value:archive_mode} and no streaming standby is connected; the RPO declaration earns no points until a continuous WAL transport exists.
on_violation.remediation: Enable archive_mode with a real archive_command, or add a streaming standby, so a continuous WAL transport backs the declared RPO. If the business truly accepts a longer recovery point, the declared rpo_target is wrong: correct it, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Aggressive RPO declared while archive_timeout does not bound it
consistency_rules.description: rpo_5/rpo_15 with WAL archiving and no streaming standby rely on archive_timeout to archive a quiet database's changes in time. At 0 (never force a switch) or above the declared RPO, recent changes can stay unarchived longer than the RPO allows. The rule stays silent when neither streaming_status nor ha_standby_count was collected: an unknown standby state never invalidates the declaration.

on_violation.title: Declared RPO {value:rpo_target} is not bounded by archive_timeout={value:archive_timeout}
on_violation.description: rpo_target={value:rpo_target} with archive_mode={value:archive_mode} and no streaming standby, but archive_timeout={value:archive_timeout} seconds; on a quiet database the last changes can stay unarchived longer than the declared RPO, so the declaration earns no points.
on_violation.remediation: Set archive_timeout to at most the declared RPO in seconds (for example 60 for rpo_5), or connect a streaming standby. If the business truly accepts a longer recovery point, the declared rpo_target is wrong: correct it, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Connection saturation amplifying lock contention
consistency_rules.description: Near-exhausted connection slots combined with blocked sessions indicate a saturation spiral: new sessions queue on locks held by sessions that cannot finish.

on_violation.title: Connections at {value:connection_usage_pct}% with {value:blocked_queries} blocked sessions
on_violation.description: connection_usage_pct={value:connection_usage_pct} and blocked_queries={value:blocked_queries}; both capacity and performance are degraded by the same saturation event.
on_violation.remediation: Add a connection pooler (or raise max_connections judiciously) and identify the lock-holding sessions (pg_blocking_pids).

consistency_rules.title: Aggressive RTO declared without tested recovery
consistency_rules.description: rto_5/rto_15 promise minutes-level recovery, which cannot be trusted unless recovery has actually been tested.

on_violation.title: Declared RTO {value:rto_target} is unproven — recovery not tested
on_violation.description: rto_target={value:rto_target} claims minutes-level recovery, but recovery_tested is not attested; the RTO declaration earns no points until recovery is validated.
on_violation.remediation: Perform and document a recovery test at the declared RTO. If the business truly accepts a longer recovery time, the declared rto_target is wrong: correct it to a horizon you can prove.

consistency_rules.title: Aggressive RTO declared without PITR, standby, or backup tooling
consistency_rules.description: An RTO of one hour or less needs at least one fast recovery path — PITR, a streaming standby, or a backup tool. With none of them present the declared RTO has no technical basis.

on_violation.title: Declared RTO {value:rto_target} is unachievable — no PITR, standby, or backup tool
on_violation.description: rto_target={value:rto_target} but no PITR, no connected streaming standby, and no recognized backup tool is present; there is no path to meet the declared RTO.
on_violation.remediation: Establish a fast recovery path (PITR, a streaming standby, or a backup tool such as pgBackRest). If the business truly accepts a longer recovery time, the declared rto_target is wrong: correct it.

consistency_rules.title: Aggressive RTO declared on a standalone instance too large to restore in time
consistency_rules.description: The declared RTO cannot be met by restoring from backup on a standalone instance: at the attested or default restore throughput the database takes more than 15 minutes to restore, and there is no HA topology to fail over to.

on_violation.title: Declared RTO {value:rto_target} not achievable by restore on a standalone instance
on_violation.description: rto_target={value:rto_target} with ha_topology=none: restoring {value:database_size} GB takes about {value:restore_time_estimate_minutes} minutes at the attested or default throughput, longer than the declared RTO.
on_violation.remediation: Add an HA topology (a standby or a managed cluster) so failover bounds the RTO, or move the large database to a dedicated instance. If the business truly accepts a longer recovery time, the declared rto_target is wrong: correct it.

consistency_rules.title: One-hour RTO declared on a standalone instance too large to restore in time
consistency_rules.description: The declared RTO cannot be met by restoring from backup on a standalone instance: at the attested or default restore throughput the database takes more than 60 minutes to restore, and there is no HA topology to fail over to.

on_violation.title: Declared RTO {value:rto_target} not achievable by restore on a standalone instance
on_violation.description: rto_target={value:rto_target} with ha_topology=none: restoring {value:database_size} GB takes about {value:restore_time_estimate_minutes} minutes at the attested or default throughput, longer than the declared RTO.
on_violation.remediation: Add an HA topology (a standby or a managed cluster) so failover bounds the RTO, or move the large database to a dedicated instance. If the business truly accepts a longer recovery time, the declared rto_target is wrong: correct it.

consistency_rules.title: Regulated posture declared with SSL/TLS off
consistency_rules.description: A regulated security posture requires encrypted client connections. SSL disabled contradicts the declaration.

on_violation.title: Regulated posture declared but SSL is off
on_violation.description: security_posture=regulated but ssl_enabled={value:ssl_enabled}; a regulated instance must encrypt client connections, so the posture declaration earns no points.
on_violation.remediation: Enable SSL/TLS (ssl = on) with valid certificates. SSL is required at every security posture, so lowering the declared posture would not remove this.

consistency_rules.title: Regulated posture declared without audit logging
consistency_rules.description: A regulated posture expects audit logging (pgAudit). Its absence contradicts the declaration.

on_violation.title: Regulated posture declared but pgAudit is not installed
on_violation.description: security_posture=regulated but pgaudit_installed is not attested; a regulated instance is expected to keep an audit trail.
on_violation.remediation: Install and configure pgAudit. If the estate is truly not regulated, the declared security_posture is wrong: correct it, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Regulated posture with short log retention
consistency_rules.description: A regulated posture implies 12-month log retention (e.g. PCI DSS v4: 12 months total, 90 days immediately available). Retention below 365 days contradicts the declaration.

on_violation.title: Regulated posture declared but log retention is {value:log_retention_days} days
on_violation.description: security_posture=regulated expects 365-day log retention; the attested retention does not meet it, so the retention metric earns no points.
on_violation.remediation: Extend log archiving or rotation to 12 months. If the estate is truly not regulated, the declared security_posture is wrong: correct it, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Growth headroom declared while storage is already critical
consistency_rules.description: A growth-headroom target implies spare storage. With disk usage already past the healthy threshold the headroom claim does not hold.

on_violation.title: Growth headroom declared but storage is already at {value:disk_usage_pct}%
on_violation.description: growth_headroom_target={value:growth_headroom_target} but disk_usage_pct={value:disk_usage_pct}%; there is no headroom to plan against.
on_violation.remediation: Add storage or reduce consumption to restore headroom, or shorten the declared growth horizon.

consistency_rules.title: Synchronous topology declared without synchronous replication configured
consistency_rules.description: Declaring a sync-standby topology requires synchronous_commit and a synchronous standby list that actually enforce it.

on_violation.title: Synchronous topology declared but not enforced
on_violation.description: ha_topology=sync_standby but synchronous_commit={value:synchronous_commit} and synchronous_standby_names_count={value:synchronous_standby_names_count}; the declared synchronous topology is not actually in force.
on_violation.remediation: Set synchronous_commit to remote_apply, remote_write or on and populate synchronous_standby_names. If the estate truly runs asynchronous replication, the declared ha_topology is wrong: correct it to async_standby, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Standby/cluster topology declared without streaming replication
consistency_rules.description: Any standby or cluster-managed topology implies streaming replication is running. No streaming status contradicts the declaration.

on_violation.title: Replication topology declared but no streaming standby is connected
on_violation.description: ha_topology={value:ha_topology} but streaming_status is not truthy; no streaming standby is observed to back the declared topology.
on_violation.remediation: Reconnect the streaming standby and confirm it streams. If the estate has no standby, the declaration is wrong: correct ha_topology to none, which lowers the target.

consistency_rules.title: Upgrade plan declared while falling multiple majors behind
consistency_rules.description: An upgrade plan that leaves the instance three or more major versions behind is not being executed.

on_violation.title: Upgrade plan declared but {value:versions_behind} major versions behind
on_violation.description: upgrade_plan={value:upgrade_plan} but versions_behind={value:versions_behind}; a plan that leaves the instance this far behind is not delivering.
on_violation.remediation: Execute the upgrade to within two majors of current, or revise the upgrade plan to reflect reality.

consistency_rules.title: No upgrade plan while falling multiple majors behind
consistency_rules.description: Declaring no upgrade plan is honest and scores full on its own, but with three or more majors behind the absence of a plan is itself a future-proofing gap (the companion to PG-CR-FUT-1, which handles a plan that is not delivering).

on_violation.title: No upgrade plan and {value:versions_behind} major versions behind
on_violation.description: upgrade_plan={value:upgrade_plan} and versions_behind={value:versions_behind}; with no plan and this many majors behind, an upgrade is overdue.
on_violation.remediation: Document an upgrade plan and schedule the move to within two majors of current.
